description: Routing, switching and the services that make a campus or enterprise network run: VLANs, access lists, DNS and DHCP, WAN links, NAT and quality of service, all configured and tested in the simulator. Taught to the depth of the industry routing-and-switching certification and a leading networking course.
modelledOn: Cisco CCNA 200-301 routing, switching and services objectives
Kurose and Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
outcomes: Configure static and dynamic routing (RIP, OSPF, basic BGP) and read routing tables and protocol state.
Design and configure VLANs, trunks, inter-VLAN routing and spanning tree on switched networks.
Write standard and extended access control lists to enforce a stated security policy.
Deploy DNS and DHCP services and troubleshoot name and address assignment faults.
Explain WAN technologies and configure PPP, Frame Relay and NAT on a border router.
Measure bandwidth, response time and reliability and apply QoS to protect voice and critical traffic.

units.title: Routing fundamentals
topics: Router architecture: interfaces, forwarding, the routing table, longest-prefix match
Static routes, default routes, administrative distance and metrics
Distance-vector routing: Bellman-Ford, RIP, count-to-infinity, split horizon
Link-state routing: Dijkstra, OSPF areas, LSAs, neighbour adjacency
Path-vector routing and BGP: autonomous systems, policies, how Ghana's ISPs peer
Configuring and verifying RIP and OSPF in Packet Tracer or GNS3

units.title: Switching
topics: Switch operation review; store-and-forward versus cut-through; MAC table ageing
Spanning Tree Protocol: root bridge, port roles, convergence; Rapid STP
EtherChannel and link aggregation
Switch security: port security, DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection

units.title: VLANs
topics: Why VLANs: broadcast domains, segmentation, security
Creating VLANs, assigning access ports, 802.1Q trunking and the native VLAN
Inter-VLAN routing: router-on-a-stick and layer-3 switches
VLAN design for a university: staff, students, labs, management, voice
Troubleshooting VLAN and trunk mismatches

units.title: Access control lists
topics: ACL logic: top-down matching, implicit deny, wildcard masks
Standard and extended numbered and named ACLs; placement rules
Applying ACLs to interfaces and to VTY lines; logging
Writing ACLs for a policy: block social media in labs, allow only web and DNS from guests
IPv6 ACLs in brief

units.title: DNS and DHCP
topics: DNS hierarchy, resolvers, authoritative servers, record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR, TXT), TTL and caching
Setting up a DNS server; split-horizon and internal zones; DNS over HTTPS in brief
DHCP discover-offer-request-acknowledge; pools, leases, reservations, options; DHCP relay
Troubleshooting name resolution and address assignment with dig, nslookup and packet capture

units.title: Basic WAN concepts
topics: WAN versus LAN; leased lines, circuit and packet-switched services, MPLS, Metro Ethernet, broadband, satellite, cellular
Serial links, DCE/DTE, clocking, CSU/DSU; HDLC
VPNs over the Internet: site-to-site and remote-access, IPsec and WireGuard in brief
WAN options for connecting branches across Ghana and their costs

units.title: Point-to-Point Protocol
topics: PPP frame, LCP and NCP phases; options negotiation
Authentication with PAP and CHAP
Configuring and verifying PPP on serial links; PPPoE for broadband
Multilink PPP and compression

units.title: Frame Relay
topics: Virtual circuits, DLCIs, LMI, Inverse ARP; hub-and-spoke topologies
Committed information rate, bursting, FECN/BECN and discard eligibility
Configuring Frame Relay point-to-point and multipoint subinterfaces; split-horizon issues
Legacy status of Frame Relay and what replaced it (MPLS, Metro Ethernet)

units.title: Network Address Translation
topics: Private addressing and the reasons for NAT; inside and outside, local and global addresses
Static NAT, dynamic NAT, PAT (overload); configuring and verifying translations
Port forwarding for hosting a server behind NAT; NAT traversal problems for VoIP and peer-to-peer
Carrier-grade NAT and IPv6 as the long-term fix

units.title: Bandwidth, response time, reliability and QoS
topics: Measuring bandwidth, latency, jitter and packet loss; iperf, ping, SNMP graphs; SLAs
Redundancy and reliability: HSRP/VRRP, link redundancy, MTBF and availability calculations
QoS models: best effort, IntServ, DiffServ; classification, marking (DSCP), queuing, policing, shaping
Configuring QoS for VoIP and video on a congested link
Capacity planning and a network design project for a campus with a WAN link to a branch

schedule.title: Routing tables, static routes and distance-vector
schedule.exercise: Given a routing table with overlapping prefixes, work out by hand which route is chosen for ten destination addresses and why, then explain count-to-infinity with a three-router example.

tasks.title: Configure static and default routes on a three-router chain so that two LANs can ping each other, and verify with traceroute
Enable RIP on four routers, then break a link and watch the routing tables converge, noting the hop counts and the time taken
Reproduce a count-to-infinity loop on a three-router topology after a link failure, then fix it with split horizon and poison reverse

schedule.title: Link-state routing, BGP and OSPF configuration
schedule.exercise: Run Dijkstra's algorithm by hand on a seven-node weighted graph from two different source routers and compare the shortest-path trees.

tasks.title: Configure single-area OSPF on three routers and verify neighbour adjacencies and the learned routes with the show commands
Build a two-area OSPF network, check that area border routers summarise routes and compare the link-state database of an internal router and an ABR
Model three autonomous systems with BGP and set a local preference so that traffic to one prefix prefers the cheaper of two upstream providers

schedule.title: Switching, spanning tree and switch security
schedule.exercise: Hand-compute the root bridge, root ports and designated ports for a four-switch triangle topology with given bridge priorities and link costs.

tasks.title: Watch a switch learn MAC addresses as hosts ping each other, read the MAC table and see an entry age out after inactivity
Connect four switches in a loop, elect the root bridge by setting priority, and identify which ports are blocking and why
Enable port security and DHCP snooping on an access switch, then attach a rogue DHCP server and confirm that the offers are blocked

schedule.title: VLANs and inter-VLAN routing
schedule.exercise: Plan a VLAN numbering and subnet scheme for a school with administration, teaching and lab networks, and justify the choices in a short table.

tasks.title: Create two VLANs on a switch, assign access ports and show that hosts in different VLANs cannot ping each other
Link two switches with an 802.1Q trunk, carry both VLANs across it and prove same-VLAN hosts on different switches can communicate
Configure router-on-a-stick sub-interfaces so that two VLANs can reach each other, then restrict traffic between them to web only

schedule.title: VLAN design and troubleshooting
schedule.exercise: Write a troubleshooting checklist for VLAN faults, then apply it in a worked example where hosts lose connectivity after a switch replacement.

tasks.title: Build a campus VLAN design with staff, student, lab and management VLANs and confirm each group reaches only the services it should
Find a trunk native VLAN mismatch from the log messages and symptoms, correct it and verify with ping across the trunk
Diagnose a network with three injected faults (wrong access VLAN, trunk allowed list, missing sub-interface) and fix them in the fewest steps

schedule.title: Access control lists
schedule.exercise: Write ACL statements, with wildcard masks, for four stated security policies and explain the placement of each ACL and the effect of the implicit deny.

tasks.title: Create a standard ACL that blocks one host and permits everyone else, apply it to an interface and check the match counters after test pings
Write an extended ACL that lets guest hosts use only web and DNS to the internet, apply it and verify blocked and allowed traffic
Design ACLs for a lab policy that blocks social media sites but allows learning sites, restricts Telnet to the admin subnet and logs every denied packet

schedule.title: DNS and DHCP
schedule.exercise: Explain the full chain of queries when a student resolves a university web address with a cold cache, labelling resolver, root, TLD and authoritative steps.

tasks.title: Query A, MX and NS records from a simulated DNS server and explain how a changed TTL affects how soon clients see an update
Configure a DHCP pool with a lease time and an exclusion range, and watch four clients receive addresses through the four-step exchange
Troubleshoot a LAN where clients get an address but cannot browse by name, using packet capture to locate the missing DNS option

schedule.title: WAN technologies and VPNs
schedule.exercise: Compare leased line, Metro Ethernet, broadband and cellular links for connecting three branch offices in Ghana, using a table of cost, speed and reliability.

tasks.title: Bring up a serial link between two routers by setting clock rate on the DCE side and verifying the line protocol turns up
Build a site-to-site tunnel between two branch routers and show that private traffic crosses the public network encapsulated
Design a hub-and-spoke WAN for a bank with a head office and four regional branches and justify the link type chosen for each branch by cost and resilience

schedule.title: PPP and authentication
schedule.exercise: Describe the PPP link establishment phases in order and explain why CHAP is stronger than PAP, using captured packets as evidence.

tasks.title: Bring up a PPP link and read the LCP negotiation exchange to see the options each side offers and accepts
Configure CHAP between two routers, then deliberately mismatch the shared secret and observe the authentication failure
Bundle two PPP links with Multilink PPP and demonstrate that traffic is balanced across both, then fail one link and keep connectivity

schedule.title: Frame Relay and legacy WAN
schedule.exercise: Write a short report explaining why Frame Relay was replaced, comparing its cost and flexibility with MPLS and Metro Ethernet.

tasks.title: Build a Frame Relay hub-and-spoke network and map the DLCIs on each router so that the hub reaches every spoke
Configure point-to-point sub-interfaces on a Frame Relay hub to fix a split-horizon routing problem and confirm spoke-to-spoke reachability
Calculate committed information rate and burst limits for a branch link, then simulate overload to see frames marked discard eligible and dropped

schedule.title: Network address translation
schedule.exercise: Explain why private addresses need NAT, and trace by hand how a PAT router rewrites the source address and port of three simultaneous connections.

tasks.title: Configure static NAT for one internal web server and verify the inside local and global address mapping in the translation table
Configure PAT with overload for a LAN of ten hosts sharing one public address and read the translation table while several hosts browse
Publish a server behind PAT by port forwarding, then diagnose why a peer-to-peer or VoIP application fails through the translating router

schedule.title: Performance, redundancy and quality of service
schedule.exercise: Calculate the availability of a link with given MTBF and MTTR, then of two such links in parallel, and state whether it meets a 99.9 percent SLA.

tasks.title: Measure round-trip time, jitter and packet loss across a link with ping and a traffic generator, and compare them with the stated SLA
Configure two routers with HSRP, fail the active router and show the standby takes over with the virtual gateway address unchanged
Mark voice traffic with a DSCP value and give it priority queuing on a congested link, then compare its delay with and without the policy

schedule.title: QoS configuration and a campus network project
schedule.exercise: Prepare the design document for a campus with a WAN branch, including addressing plan, VLAN list, routing choice, security policy and capacity estimate.

tasks.title: Configure QoS on a congested WAN link so that a video call stays smooth while a large file transfer runs, and verify queue statistics
Estimate bandwidth needs for a campus and branch from user counts and application mix, then choose link speeds and check them under simulated load
Design, build and test a campus network with VLANs, OSPF, ACLs, NAT and a branch WAN link, and show it passes a ten-point acceptance checklist
